clue.text: Stop right there and use a ruler?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: set a limit beyond which you will not go
second meaning, taken literally: mark a straight stroke on paper

explanation.surface: A teacher snaps at a pupil to halt and get out a straight edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for refusing to go further is also exactly what you do with a ruler and pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to set a limit and refuse anything beyond it, while literally it describes ruling a straight mark.

clue.text: Play whose characters go just beyond Quebec and India?

parts.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the word just after Quebec (Q) is Romeo (R)
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the word just after India (I) is Juliet (J)

explanation.surface: A quiz question about a play whose cast seems to travel past a Canadian province and an Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters here are letters of the alphabet: the NATO code words one step past Quebec and India are the two lovers' names.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of the star-crossed lovers of Verona is a famous stage drama.

clue.text: Upward surge for wild animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, going upward means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a surge is a rush or flow of water

explanation.surface: A sudden rise in numbers of some wild creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey hunter of forests and tundra is a classic untamed beast that roams in packs.

clue.text: Lift thing he moved round back of house

indicators.note: letters that are moved round are shifted into a different order
the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end is kept

explanation.surface: A man pushing some object around behind his home.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something, as in raising spirits or a level, is to make it higher; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Rubbish kittens, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: refuse dropped in public places

definitions.note: a collective noun for a brood of young
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a group of young animals born together, kittens being one example

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses kittens as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means scattered refuse and also a set of young born to one mother at one time.

clue.text: Home near Exeter seems tiny, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: An estate agent's remark that a house by a Devon city looks small.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's nest is its dwelling, and the word is used loosely for any cosy residence.

clue.text: Appetisers with pork warmed up?

parts.note: setter's reading: the pork animals themselves tucked under bedding to keep warm

explanation.walkthrough: The dish is small sausages wrapped in bacon, a British Christmas favourite; the name pictures animals snug under bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of these party nibbles describes sausages wrapped in bacon or pastry, served as starters or Christmas sides.

clue.text: Show mattered, son performing

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are putting on an act and moving about into new positions

explanation.surface: A proud parent says the show was important because their son was in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to display or prove it, which is the verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Part of food processor in a mess, little pumpkin ultimately churned up

indicators.note: churned up means stirred violently so the letters lose their order
ultimately points to the final letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A kitchen blender clogged up with pulped pumpkin.
explanation.walkthrough: The food processor is the body, not a kitchen gadget, and 'in a mess' is fodder rather than a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This section of the gut digests and absorbs nutrients, so it is a component of the body's digestive machinery.

clue.text: Immutable, as stone flying through the air, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fixed rules that cannot be changed

definitions.text: as stone flying through the air, perhaps
definitions.note: describes the stone, an adjective phrase
definitions.meaning: second meaning, literally: a thrown stone is solid and moving at speed

explanation.surface: Something as unchangeable as a hurled rock.
explanation.walkthrough: The fixed phrase for rules is split into its parts: a stone is solid, and in flight it is quick.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes rules or facts that are rigid and allow no exceptions or change.

clue.text: Fragrant resin all gone, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means take the letters in the first, third, fifth and seventh positions

parts.note: the odd letters of these two words

explanation.surface: The perfumed gum has run out completely.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides the succulent plant, the word names the fragrant wood or resin of an eastern tree, as in the Bible's myrrh and aloes.
explanation.definitionFit: In older and biblical usage the word names aromatic agarwood resin used in incense and perfume.

clue.text: One pilfered by the felon, originally — here's the culprit!

indicators.note: something pilfered is taken in by the robber, so it ends up held inside the other letters
originally points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Pointing out the criminal who took something.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside THE plus F, after the H, giving T-H-I-E-F.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person responsible for a wrong, and in a case of pilfering that person is a robber.

clue.text: Old second line heading for Omani capital

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
S is the abbreviation for second
L is the abbreviation for line

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An old route that leads to the capital of Oman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Omani capital' reads as one phrase, pointing to Muscat; the capital is in Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Norway, the seat of its government.

clue.text: A king, in retiring, all of a quiver

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word that follows

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch trembling as he abdicates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like a king stepping down; here it simply means bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all of a quiver means trembling, and trembling hands or legs are unsteady.

clue.text: Card game with tricks finally played

indicators.note: letters that are played with are moved about into a fresh arrangement
finally points to the end letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A card game in which tricks are won, played to the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricks' and 'played' fit the game so well that they look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This trick-taking pastime for four players in partnerships is a classic game played with a pack of cards.

clue.text: Small boats welcome in new design

indicators.note: in places the preceding piece inside the following one
new means the letters of the following word are made over into another order

parts.note: hi is a word of greeting

explanation.surface: A boatyard welcomes a fresh design for little craft.
explanation.definitionFit: These are little open boats for rowing or sailing, often carried as tenders by larger vessels.

clue.text: Calls received by Telegraph, one sarcastic

indicators.note: received by means held within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Remarks taken by the newspaper, one of them biting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is the British newspaper that publishes this puzzle, a nice self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone is to ring them, so the verb is a synonym for making telephone calls.

clue.text: Half opting twice for train

indicators.note: twice means the same piece is written two times in a row
half means only the front portion is kept and the rest dropped

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly choosing a train, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a child's word for a steam train.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the nursery word for a railway engine, imitating the puffing sound it makes.

clue.text: One struggling to keep Jack in good health — it's serious

indicators.note: to keep means to hold the following pieces inside
struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
someone who is OK is well

explanation.surface: A carer struggling to keep someone called Jack well, which is no laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is no laughing matter is the same as calling it grave rather than trivial.

clue.text: Artist's boiling kettle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: James McNeill ..., the American painter
second meaning: a kettle on the boil gives off a shrill whistle

explanation.surface: A painter's kettle on the boil.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler is best known for the portrait often called Whistler's Mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname is that of a famous American painter, and it also describes anything that whistles, as a hot kettle does.

clue.text: Dance with two beers?

wordplay.note: a can is a tin of beer, and two of them side by side

explanation.surface: Dancing after a couple of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The high-kicking French music-hall routine is a lively stage dance.

clue.text: Fabric considered

definitions.meaning: second meaning: believed or judged, past tense

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a pressed woollen textile and also the past tense of a verb meaning to hold an opinion.

clue.text: Old German boy has stolen a kiss

indicators.note: whoever has stolen something holds it, so the following letters go inside

parts.note: X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A long-ago German lad snatched a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saxons were an early Germanic people, some of whom settled in Britain.

clue.text: Join idiot in conversation?

indicators.note: in conversation means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a nit is a fool, and the silent K makes the answer sound identical

explanation.surface: An invitation to talk with a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken bones knit together, so the verb can mean to unite or bond firmly.

clue.text: Necessary requirement for story in bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the storyline that every novel needs
second meaning: a patch of garden ground

explanation.surface: A bedtime story needs something to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative needs a sequence of events, the storyline, and a small piece of garden land for planting has the same name.

clue.text: Note remaining briefly, musical symbol

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: what is remaining is what is left

explanation.surface: A short note hanging on, then a notation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The sign at the start of a stave fixes the pitch of the lines, a basic mark of musical notation.

clue.text: Solver with shellshock, more distraught

indicators.note: someone distraught is badly upset, and the letters are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: A crossword fan suffering from battle trauma and getting more upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solver' suggests a puzzler like you; it is the fictional detective who solves cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's famous detective solves mysteries, so he is a solver of crimes.

clue.text: Cold counter with cod, plaice etc?

parts.note: a stand is a stall or counter
read as 'of fish': a counter holding cod

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's slab displaying cod and plaice.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as STAND OF FISH, a fishmonger's display.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is aloof and unfriendly, which is what the hyphenated adjective describes.
